content.title: About
content.content: Sambar is a traditional South Indian vegetable stew made with lentils, beans, pumpkin, carrots, tomatoes and a blend of spices. It is served hot, often alongside rice, dosa, idli or vada.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sambar is considered the “protein‑rich” component of a typical South Indian thali.
Recipes differ by region: Tamil Nadu uses more tamarind, while Karnataka adds coconut paste.
Tamarind gives sambar its characteristic tangy‑sweet flavor.
It is often cooked in large communal pots (sambar‑pots) for festivals and gatherings.
The dish can be completely vegan when prepared without ghee or butter.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Lentils and beans provide a complete set of amino acids essential for muscle and tissue health.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Vegetables and legumes support healthy digestion and promote satiety.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Tamarind, carrots and tomatoes contain vitamin B6 and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Sambar raises blood sugar slowly, making it suitable for people with pre‑diabetes.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Tomatoes and spices such as turmeric and coriander provide antioxidants that combat free radicals.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to lentils or beans.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Adding excessive salt or ready‑made seasoning mixes can make the dish too salty.

items.title: Tamarind acidity
items.content: Large amounts of tamarind may irritate the stomach in people with gastritis.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot sambar over rice or with dosa, idli, or vada. Garnish with fresh cilantro, a squeeze of lime, and toasted lentils for extra crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat to a rolling boil before serving to ensure safety.
